reference.title: Standing Scapula Rotation (male)
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the shoulders lift and draw back, breathe out as they lower and come forward.

prescription.tempo: Slow and smooth, about 3 s per circle
prescription.frequency: Daily or as a warm-up before upper-body training
prescription.progression: Larger circles, then add a light band or hold light dumbbells

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, arms hanging relaxed by the sides.
Lift the shoulders toward the ears, squeeze the shoulder blades back and together, press them down, then let them glide forward: one smooth circle.
Again, as big and as slow as is comfortable; the arms stay relaxed and the head still.
Settle the shoulders in neutral; repeat, or reverse the direction.

mistakes.fix: Keep the chin level; only the shoulder blades move.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the elbows or swinging the arms
mistakes.fix: Let the arms hang; they ride along with the shoulder blades.
Slow, full circles: up, back, down, forward.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back to squeeze back
mistakes.fix: Ribs down; the movement is at the shoulder blades.

kinematics.norm: Shoulders rise toward the ears and press down below neutral (clinical opinion)
Blades squeeze back and together, then glide forward; retraction exercises move the clavicle back by about 15-18 degrees (Oyama 2010)

sources.title: GymVisual #17583, Standing Scapula Rotation (male), video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)
Ekstrom, Donatelli and Soderberg 2003, surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp pain, clicking with pain, or tingling down the arm.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
A mobility and warm-up drill: low load, not a strength builder on its own.
modify: Neck discomfort: smaller lift toward the ears, focus on back and down.
Seated version if standing balance is a problem.

muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upper trapezius and levator scapulae lift the shoulders toward the ears (clinical opinion; shrug-type elevation strongly activates the upper trapezius, Ekstrom 2003).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upper trapezius and levator scapulae lift the shoulders toward the ears (clinical opinion; shrug-type elevation strongly activates the upper trapezius, Ekstrom 2003).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Rhomboids and middle trapezius draw the blades back and together; retraction drills activate them (Oyama 2010).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Rhomboids and middle trapezius draw the blades back and together; retraction drills activate them (Oyama 2010).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Serratus anterior glides the blades forward around the ribcage (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Serratus anterior glides the blades forward around the ribcage (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Lats and lower trapezius pull the blades down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Lats and lower trapezius pull the blades down (clinical opinion).
